title: POC Weekly: Integration Adapters, Function Calling, Output Contracts
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint focused on SDK adapter patterns, function-calling edge cases, and stabilizing structured output. We reviewed recent test runs (latency/cost tradeoffs), discussed a recurring mismatch in output schema, and agreed on a short set of experiments: enforce schema validation in the SDK, add a small retry/backoff for tool calls, and run a 24h canary with dedicated quantized model variant. Redwood to share benchmark sheet + updated SDK snippet; Atlas to provide failing prompt set and grant sandbox access to a staging route.
next_steps: Redwood: share updated SDK adapter example + guidance doc by 2026-07-23 (link to deck in notes)
Atlas: upload failing prompt set and example outputs by 2026-07-22 to shared drive
Ethan to run 24h canary on quantized variant (q4_3) and post latency/cost CSV by 2026-07-28
Schedule security review for Private deployment options if canary passes - target week of 2026-08-03
action_items: Sofia Martinez - Send benchmark spreadsheet and SDK snippet - due 2026-07-23
Carlos Mendes - Provide failing prompt set and example outputs - due 2026-07-22
Ethan Li - Run 24h canary with quantized model variant and share logs - due 2026-07-28
Ben Patel - Confirm KMS/HSM requirements and share high level constraints - due 2026-07-27
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Atlas PM), Carlos (Atlas BE), Maya (Atlas DS), Ben (Atlas Sec), Sam (intern)

Summary (auto): quick sync on adapter patterns, function calling, schema regression. Some audio dropouts around 00:12-00:14.

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off - this is our weekly POC checkpoint for Atlas Retail. quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya here.
[00:14] Carlos Mendes: Carlos on backend.
[00:18] Maya Johnson: Maya - DS.
[00:20] Ben Patel: Ben - security.
[00:22] Sam: Sam.
[00:24] Sofia Martinez: Awesome. Ethan, you want to run the agenda?
[00:27] Ethan Li: Yeah, sure. Today we'll cover three things: adapter patterns in the SDK we shipped, function/tool calling reliability (we've seen a few timeouts), and the structured output contract failures Maya flagged. Then quick plan for the canary.
[00:42] Priya Nair: Sounds good. We also added a new acceptance criterion around deterministic keys in the JSON output, so want to make sure that stays stable.
[00:50] Ethan Li: Right. Quick note — the SDK now has an 'adapter' abstraction that sits between your service and the Redwood client. It lets you declare a schema and will attempt to coerce outputs, but it's opt-in because coercion can mask model drift.
[01:05] Carlos Mendes: Quick question on that, will the adapter run client-side or on the invocation layer? We prefer to keep minimal logic in the client.
[01:12] Ethan Li: It's implemented in the SDK as a plugin so it runs where you run the SDK. For server apps we expect it server-side; you can also move validation to a gateway.
[01:22] Maya Johnson: We definitely want server-side. We observed that the model was sometimes returning 'null' for sku_id in edge cases which breaks downstream pipelines.
[01:32] Sofia Martinez: Can you show an example?
[01:34] Maya Johnson: Yeah, Carlos — did you upload that failing prompt to the shared folder?
[01:38] Carlos Mendes: I did, it's under /atlas/poc/failing_examples/sku_null.json, I can paste a link after.
[01:44] (link posted in chat)
[01:46] Ethan Li: I pulled it earlier — looks like a tokenization boundary + KV cache issue in longer contexts. Sometimes the model drops the prefix for the SKU extraction prompt when continuous batching is used. It's rare but reproducible.
[02:02] Ben Patel: Are we sure this is a model/serving thing and not our preprocessing? We had a whitespace normalization change last week.
[02:10] Carlos Mendes: We validated — same behavior when feeding raw input.
[02:15] Ethan Li: To be explicit, we saw two failure modes: 1) empty/null field, 2) truncated array when the output exceeds the single-token length and batching compresses it oddly.
[02:29] Priya Nair: Hmm. Could the adapter coerce to a default SKU or should we fail fast?
[02:35] Sofia Martinez: Our recommendation is fail-fast with a clear error tag you can filter on, then use a retry/alternative model path. Coercion risks silent bad data.
[02:45] Maya Johnson: Agreed, but for downstream idempotency we need consistent error tags in the JSON so we can reconcile.
[02:52] Ethan Li: We can add an errorCode field and a stable schema version to the output. The SDK will include schema version in metadata for each call.
[03:02] (short pause)
[03:08] Sofia Martinez: On the function calling side — we've seen timeouts in tool invocation when calling external microservices via function call hooks. Carlos, do you have logs?
[03:15] Carlos Mendes: Yes, I pasted a small sample in the chat. We had two timeouts around 11:14 and 11:37 server time; both took ~8s to complete and the Redwood client timed out at the default 5s.
[03:28] Ethan Li: Default SDK timeout is conservative to preserve latency SLOs. For tool calls we recommend a layered retry: immediate short retry (200-500ms jitter), then a longer backoff and mark the response as degraded. Also an idempotency token so retries aren't double-applied.
[03:44] Ben Patel: From security perspective, if retries are happening we need to ensure tokens aren't leaked to third parties and are rotated per invocation. Does the SDK surface token scoping?
[03:54] Ethan Li: Yes — we added token scoping in the 0.9.3 SDK: you can scope tokens to a route and set TTL. For Private deployments you'll get mTLS options and KMS integrations. Ben, we'll send the KMS integration note.
[04:06] Ben Patel: Please do. Also need details on audit logs retention.
[04:11] Sofia Martinez: We'll include the audit log retention matrix in the security pack.
[04:15] Sam (intern): Quick dumb question — what's q4_3 again?
[04:18] Maya Johnson: Quantized 4-bit, variant 3.
[04:20] Sam: Ah okay.
[04:22] Ethan Li: On performance: we ran a quick benchmark last night comparing the quantized variant (q4_3) to the full float variant on 512 token contexts. Median latency dropped ~18% and per-token cost down ~33% but tail latency increased slightly under continuous batching. I can post the CSV.
[04:40] Priya Nair: That matches our cost targets if we can keep the tail under control.
[04:46] Ethan Li: For tail, we recommend a small dedicated pool for hot routes or dynamic routing: low-latency route vs cost route. You can set routing policies per workspace in Console.
[04:58] Carlos Mendes: If we go dedicated, what's the minimum commit and SLA?
[05:03] Sofia Martinez: We'll send the Dedicated plan summary — monthly minimum and SLA details. For pilot you can use hosted with reserved pool bursts.
[05:10] Priya Nair: Back to the structured output regressions — Maya, can you describe the mismatch pattern?
[05:15] Maya Johnson: Sure. Most failures are subtle schema drift: keys reordered, sometimes extra keys, sometimes types changed (string vs integer). Our downstream parsers are strict.
[05:25] Ethan Li: Couple of mitigations: 1) enforce strict JSON schema in the SDK adapter and reject bad outputs, returning an explicit validation error; 2) add normalization layer that maps older schema versions to the current one; 3) run evaluation tests as part of pre-release pipeline — Redwood can run batch evals against the model on your prompt set.
[05:41] Priya Nair: We prefer 1 + 3. Reject bad outputs and run nightly evals — if drift occurs, automatic rollback to previous model version.
[05:51] Sofia Martinez: That aligns with Redwood Optimize. We can wire an eval job to alert on regression thresholds.
[05:58] Carlos Mendes: One practical ask — can the SDK include a lightweight snapshot of the schema so engineers can assert locally?
[06:04] Ethan Li: Yes, we'll add a 'schema.json' artifact in the SDK package and a CLI validator.
[06:10] Maya Johnson: Perfect. Also, when the model returns additional unknown keys, we want them kept in an 'extra' object rather than at top-level.
[06:18] Ethan Li: Noted — default will be to tuck unknowns under _extra unless you enable permissive mode.
[06:25] (pause, typing)
[06:30] Sofia Martinez: Let's talk about the canary: Ethan you proposed a 24h canary on q4_3 with a small fraction of traffic and a fallback policy. Walk through the plan.
[06:39] Ethan Li: Plan: route 5% of reads to quantized variant for 24h, monitor latencies, error rate, and schema validation failures. If any of the thresholds (error rate >0.6% or schema fails >0.2%) trigger, traffic falls back automatically to the float variant. We'll capture full logs to S3 for the window.
[06:57] Priya Nair: We need to ensure PII redaction in the logs.
[07:02] Ben Patel: And ensure logs are region-resident — can't cross EU/US boundaries for some customers.
[07:07] Ethan Li: We'll annotate logs with region tags and you can set retention and region policies in Console; Redwood Private can guarantee on-prem or VPC routing.
[07:16] Carlos Mendes: One more thing — we saw a weird substitution in outputs where 'Redwood' became 'Red wood' in a few responses; is that possible?
[07:24] Sofia Martinez: Yeah transcription/model output artifacts sometimes split tokens. It's a tokenizer/LM quirk — not an infrastructure bug. We can add a post-processing rule in the adapter to correct known entity tokenizations.
[07:36] Maya Johnson: Ok good.
[07:38] (short audio dropout 07:40-07:42)
[07:44] Sam (intern): Sorry, can I check about retries again? If we do immediate retry, won't that blow up our downstream ops?
[07:50] Ethan Li: That's why we recommend idempotency tokens and a bounded retry policy: 1 immediate retry with jitter, then mark degraded and either use cached response or return a controlled error to the app.
[07:59] Priya Nair: For acceptance criteria, we need to see <0.5% schema failures and median latency under 220ms for the hot route.
[08:08] Sofia Martinez: Noted. We'll map these into the evaluation dashboards.
[08:12] Ethan Li: Action items recap: Sofia will send SDK snippet + benchmark CSV; Ethan runs canary; Carlos provides failing prompts; Ben will confirm KMS needs.
[08:23] Priya Nair: Quick question about cost attribution — can we get token-level breakdown by route?
[08:28] Sofia Martinez: Yes, Console has per-route token billing CSV, we'll share an example export.
[08:33] Maya Johnson: Also please include example parse logs for the schema validator so our SREs can see failure payloads.
[08:40] Sofia Martinez: We'll include that.
[08:42] (five minute discussion about schedule for security review omitted)
[13:55] Sofia Martinez: Ok wrapping up, any other blockers?
[13:58] Carlos Mendes: None from infra.
[14:00] Priya Nair: No blockers.
[14:02] Maya Johnson: Quick note — can you enable a staging route with the same routing policy so we can run internal tests?
[14:08] Ethan Li: Yes we'll provision a staging route that mirrors production for the canary.
[14:12] Sofia Martinez: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send notes and action items.
[14:16] Meeting end.
